short: Assessment of Ti-6Al-4V particles as a reinforcement for AZ3
title: Assessment of Ti-6Al-4V particles as a reinforcement for AZ31 magnesium alloy-based composites to boost ductility incorporated through friction stir processing

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Ceramic-particle (e.g. SiC) reinforced Mg composites lose much of their ductility.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Ti-6Al-4V particles are spread homogeneously through the stir zone without clusters or particle-free regions. Particle/matrix interface is continuous and void-free.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Severe hot deformation in FSP drives dynamic recrystallisation. Load transfer across bonded interfaces, Orowan bowing, dislocation strain fields and Hall-Petch refinement strengthen the composite together.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (MEC/pathway), n13 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n16 (MEC/pathway). Premises: FSP of Mg alloys refines grains by dynamic recrystallisation and raises high-angle boundary fraction [19,34]; Hall-Petch relation: strength rises as grain size falls; Orowan strengthening: dislocations bow around dispersed particles; Ti-6Al-4V deforms plastically and conducts heat, unlike ceramic particles

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: AZ31/Ti-6Al-4V keeps 9-14.5% elongation where AZ31B/SiC composites reach only ~2.6-6.6%. FSP-incorporated Ti-6Al-4V raises AZ31 strength with a moderate ductility loss, far below ceramic-particle composites
states.detail: Absorbed: n20 (DSC/comparison), n21 (DSC/conclusion). Premises: AZ31B/SiC composites of Subramani et al. [39] as ductility comparator
